summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -5 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk 0; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +2.7%; weakest: Sugar #11 -12.8%. Key releases ahead: US Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks (11-16 12:00 PM ET); US Core Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US FOMC Meeting Minutes (11-18 2:00 PM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.15% (-4 bp in a month), 2-year 4.88% (+6 bp); 2s10s curve +27 bp (-10 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.13% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.56 (+1.7% in a month, +5.4% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.780 (+13.4% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.653 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.58 (+0.7%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.5% in a month (+9.1% YTD); VIX 21.2. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 86.43 $/bbl (-12.7% in a month), Brent 93.38, ULSD 4.128 $/gal (-12.6%), natural gas 3.13 (-7.5%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -8.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.1%, Hang Seng -1.8%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -10.3% in a month; gold -7.5%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
